newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond tender seen a 50/50 chance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond tender seen a 50/50 chance.

text.p: The Australian bond market could see its first Treasury bond tender of the fiscal year this week, possibly amounting to A$600 to A$700 million, traders said.

"It's about time to get the programme under way with one month already gone, but they (the Treasury) aren't desperate for the funds as yet, so there is a 50/50 feel whether they will go this week," one trader said.
The Australian Treasury told Reuters last week that with the federal budget out of the way it was likely to come to the market any time soon.
"There's a reasonable chance of a tender, and probably in the 2008 stock and a shorter one as well," another trader added.
However, a third trader said he was not expecting a tender for another week or two.
If the Treasury does go ahead this week, details of the offering will be announced at 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT) today for tender on Tuesday.
In the budget papers last week the the Treasury projected aggregate bond issuance to be around A$6.0 to A$7.0 billion for the 1996/97 year, down from A$7.8 billion in 1996/96.
This projection provides scope for a new benchmark line of stock and possibly a 2009 stock.
Funding will again be weighted to the first half of the financial year, and tenders will continue to be held every four to six weeks.
The last tender was held on June 18 when A$300 million of March 1999 and A$200 million October 2000 bonds were offered.
